scope: Kalshi BTC/ETH historical 15-minute binary settlement probabilities; exploratory development only
failures_and_reruns: Initial materialization encountered missing settlement_ms in the W4/W5 table; that file was excluded entirely from training/scoring. Empty panel acquisition refused.
Initial method 03 produced zero forecasts because two same-node derived expressions referenced newly created fields. This run is invalid despite pipeline exit 0; retained artifacts were not counted.
Corrected interactions and added exact common-row writer guards. Regression tests first showed 2 expected failures in earlier configurations, then passed after guards were applied.

Methods 01 and 02 were technically rerun with unchanged predictions after census guards; methods 01-05 were rerun with expanded output files following the owner clarification. Paired means and row identities were checked identical.
No post-July rows were trained/scored here. Prior W4/W5 research informed design. Protected forward labels, trading tests, execution, deployment and the full test suite were not used.

Iteration 04 Bayesian ridge with bounded correction improved log loss -0.000753 and Brier -0.000176, with negative loss deltas in all three bands and an incremental gain over calibrated market (-0.000532, adjusted p=.0204). Test automatic relevance determination: feature-specific Bayesian shrinkage may remove unstable activity and volatility predictors while keeping useful GRU and lead information. Preserve its 50 percent bounded blend for a cleaner comparison. Reporting-only rerun following the owner clarification: add complete per-lead, asset/lead and lead/bin calibration files, including raw-market and calibrated-market comparisons. Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 05 feature-specific Bayesian shrinkage improved log loss -0.000804 and Brier -0.000192, beating calibrated market by -0.000583 (adjusted p=.0114), with all three bands negative. Test a different feature-selection mechanism: elastic net with predominantly L1 shrinkage. It may remove weak predictors more decisively; retain the same bounded 50 percent blend. Include all owner-required cell, lead and calibration output files.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 06 elastic-net feature selection improved all three bands (overall log loss -0.000781; calibrated-market delta -0.000560). Sparse linear means appear useful. Try the new robust-loss hypothesis: Huber regression downweights unusually large market residuals, with a more conservative 25 percent bounded blend. Because binary-outcome residuals contain legitimate surprises, this is explicitly a falsification test: robust fitting may harm probability calibration.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 07 robust linear fitting improved -0.000508 log loss but missed the adjusted global screen and was weaker than Bayesian sparsity. Return to conditional-mean residuals and test a shallow regression tree: three split levels, at least 3000 training observations per leaf, and 25 percent bounded market correction. This asks whether broad localized feature regimes are more stable than a global linear slope; it is not an honest-split causal tree.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 08 shallow partitions improved all three bands and one adjusted cell, but overall incremental gain beyond market calibration was inconclusive. Test bagged random forests to reduce single-tree split variance: 80 trees, depth 5, at least 1500 rows per leaf, random feature subsets, and the same 25 percent bounded correction. This tests stable nonlinear averaging rather than a larger unanchored classifier.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 09 random forests improved log loss -0.000477 with steady negative band deltas and two adjusted cells, but added no clear improvement over market-only calibration. Test extremely randomized trees: random split thresholds may reduce optimization of noisy boundaries and diversify the residual ensemble. Keep broad leaves and the same 25 percent bounded market correction.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 10 random thresholds reduced variance and found three adjusted cells but weakened average improvement to -0.000317, mostly explainable by market calibration. Test staged histogram boosting of the probability residual under squared-error loss: 80 small updates, seven leaves, strong L2, broad leaves and no random early stopping. Unlike the previously tested direct histogram classifier, this learns only market probability error and uses a fixed 25 percent bounded correction.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 11 histogram residual boosting yielded stable raw-market gains (-0.000423 log loss) but no clear gain beyond calibrated market. Test a distinct robust boosting approach: Huber-loss gradient boosting with shallow depth-2 trees and stochastic subsampling. This asks whether reducing sensitivity to large residuals helps nonlinear models even though robust linear fitting was weaker; keep a 25 percent bounded correction and retain failures.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 12 robust shallow boosting improved -0.000589 log loss and beat calibrated market (adjusted p=.0176), suggesting local nonlinear effects may help. Test a structurally different nonparametric approach: average the market residual among 1000 earlier neighbors in market probability, GRU disagreement, lead and asset. Restricting the metric to four pre-scaled causal features avoids the unstable large feature space; keep 25 percent bounded correction.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 13 nearest-neighbor residuals gave stable raw-market improvement (-0.000476) and three adjusted cells, but no clear incremental gain over recalibration. Test direct log-loss fitting under a monotonic constraint on the market-logit feature, holding the other transformed features fixed. LightGBM uses only six inputs, seven leaves and a 10 percent blend into raw market. This preserves market ranking locally while allowing limited nonlinear correction; it is distinct from unconstrained classifiers already tested.

Fresh estimator per 30-day block; only labels published at least one full day earlier. No random early-stopping validation. Iteration 14 direct monotone classification worsened log loss +0.000340 in every historical band even with only a 10 percent blend; monotonicity alone does not preserve the information already in market probabilities. Return to the successful residual target, using LightGBM leaf-wise squared-error fitting with both L1 and L2 leaf penalties, broad leaves and a 25 percent bounded correction. This tests sparse nonlinear corrections instead of replacing the market forecast.
